plain: A satellite measure of how green and dense the vegetation is. Low values suggest bare soil.
A run of days with almost no rain. Long dry spells during flowering can cut yield.
How much water is held in the root zone. NASA POWER estimates this from satellite and weather models.
The first reliable start of the rainy season: enough rain to wet the soil, with no long dry spell straight after.
A ten-day period: days 1 to 10, 11 to 20, or 21 to the end of the month. There are 36 in a year.
The share of seasons in which rainfall, dry spells and heat all stayed within a crop's limits.
A what-if run with less rain or more heat. It shows how rankings react; it is not a forecast.
How much we trust a location's numbers. A single data source is labelled Medium until a second satellite source agrees.
